Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Body, health & movement

suck verb

also sucking, suck your thumb, suck out

classical

Cic. N.D. 2.122: alia sūgunt, alia carpunt
Varr. RR 2.1.20: mātris sūgunt mammam (Lewis & Short)

sūgō, sūgere, sūxī, sūctum

verb, third conjugation

Other words

  • exsūgō, exsūgere, exsūxī, exsūctum — suck out

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cato Agr. 156.3; Plaut. Epid. 2.2.5 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • nam tunc sūgere nōram et adquiēscere dēlectātiōnibus, flēre autem offēnsiōnēs carnis meae, nihil amplius

    for then I knew how to suck, and to settle when I was content, and to cry when my body was hurt; nothing moreAug. Conf. 1.6.7

  • Nōlī pollicem sūgere.

    Don’t suck your thumb.composed

See also lick, drink.

SourcesLewis & Short: sugo · Lewis & Short: exsugo

Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-augustinus), checked against the editions named there.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
